intents.rationale: No body limit middleware exists; add starlette/middleware/body_limit.py.
413 enforcement must be added in the new middleware.
Content-Length fail-fast plus byte counting is new.
Starlette, Router, Mount, Route have no max_body_size parameter.
Scoping/override logic is new: outer-most middleware at app level, inner wrappers adjust the effective limit.
Temp files are only closed on MultiPartException/OSError; must close on any interruption.
Docs must describe the option and middleware.

criteria.text: RequestBodyLimitMiddleware(app, max_body_size=N) wraps any ASGI app; with None or no limit all bodies pass; bytes received from the server (incl. chunked, no Content-Length) are counted.
A body exceeding the limit yields 413 with plain-text body 'Content Too Large'; if the app already started its response, no second response is sent and receive() returns http.disconnect.
Declared Content-Length over limit gives 413 without the app reading the body; missing or understated Content-Length is still enforced on actual bytes.
Starlette, Router, Mount and Route accept max_body_size (default None = unlimited) and enforce it.
App-level limit applies before routing; inner router/mount/route limits override the outer limit both raising and lowering it.
Multipart bodies (file data and encoding overhead) count toward the limit, and multipart temp files are closed on any interrupted parse including crossing the limit.
docs/middleware.md, docs/applications.md and docs/routing.md document max_body_size and RequestBodyLimitMiddleware.

tasks.summary: Order: (1) add starlette/middleware/body_limit.py: middleware wraps receive/send once per request, counts bytes, checks Content-Length up-front, on overflow sends 413 'Content Too Large' via PlainTextResponse if not started, then returns http.disconnect from receive and drops later sends; the wrapper state is kept in scope so an inner middleware instance only changes the effective limit (raise or lower) instead of re-wrapping. (2) Add max_body_size to Router, Mount, Route (wrap their app via the middleware only when not None) and Starlette (put the middleware outermost, outside ServerErrorMiddleware). (3) In formparsers close files on any exception (BaseException) during parse. (4) Tests, then docs.
